abbotsford_guide.text: Welcome to Abbotsford, which is not so much a house as a very large hobby. What shall I tell you?

then.text: Scott was a lawyer and poet before he turned novelist: Waverley, Rob Roy, Ivanhoe. He was so popular that his books made him a fortune, and he spent it here, which in the end was rather the trouble.

The house is stuffed with curiosities: Rob Roy's gun and sporran, a sword of the Marquess of Montrose, Napoleon's pen case, armour and antlers, and a library of around 9,000 books. Scott collected everything with a story attached.

In 1822 Scott stage-managed George IV's visit to Edinburgh, the first by a reigning monarch in nearly two centuries, and persuaded everyone to turn out in tartan. The King wore a kilt, in bright pink tights. The result was a craze for tartan that has never quite stopped.
Scott's great deerhound Maida is carved in stone by the front door, with a Latin epitaph Scott wrote himself. He loved his dogs, and kept a houseful, so the stone is about the right size for the job.
Come back any time. History keeps.
